_readme: rail produce prompt modules — the pinned production bible (FLYWHEEL pinned strategy).
Families copied verbatim 2026-07-11 from the Content Lab prompt_library.seed.json
(itself seeded from ocean-agents content-agent; MASTER-PROMPTS.md + LAWS.md in the
Obsidian prompt-lab are the human-readable source of truth). Edit slots/menus here;
the composer fills {slot} placeholders deterministically with no repeated combination.
providers.*.replicate_model may be overridden without code changes (Lab pattern).
keepers_per_gen are PLANNING rates from real runs: truck complete-frame vertical fit 1.0/gen
2026-07-09 delivered run), ugc 0.27 (why it is PARKED), boat unproven -> 0.70 assumed.
COST MODEL (rail supply --fleet / FLEET_SUPPLY_GOAL.md, git history): a post consumes one KEEPER clip, so
the unit economic is cost_per_keeper = provider.cost_per_gen_usd / family.keepers_per_gen.
This is IDENTICAL to what produce.rs actually spends (gens = ceil(keepers/keepers_per_gen),
cost = gens*cost_per_gen), so the forecast can never drift from the generator. There is NO
clips_per_gen divisor: a generated candidate is not a keeper — keepers_per_gen already measures
how many candidates survive QA. keepers_per_gen is the UNMETERED yield knob Eric sets from live
runs; for a capital forecast the default is CONSERVATIVE (truck 1.0/gen -> $0.50/keeper at the
list gen price). cost_per_gen_usd 0.50 is a list-price placeholder (~$0.28 observed);
meter it. Formats with no family (POV pages) report UNKNOWN — excluded from $, never guessed.

VISUAL RESET 2026-07-22: WINNER_VISUAL_REFERENCE.md is the admission authority. The active truck family returns to dark, muted, natural early iPhone-winner scenes; washed-out daylight, orange-desert, and sharp/crisp product-render output are rejected.

truck.fixed_subject: a clean recognizable dark navy-black full-size crew-cab pickup with natural factory-like proportions, normal panel seams and handles, plain unmarked dark wheels, clear empty windows with no visible occupants, and no readable lettering or license plate
truck.quality_guards: low wheel-height front-quarter, rear-quarter, or natural near-side view; the complete truck and meaningful surrounding landscape remain readable throughout; the truck is parked and completely stationary with its wheels and tires not rotating; moody low-exposure phone footage with deep blacks, controlled highlights, natural softness, preserved shadow detail, and muted color; no milky haze, pale high-key daylight, or washed-out grade; plain unmarked vehicle surfaces, no visible occupants, no readable lettering or plates
truck.template: Extreme wide low wheel-height {angle} of {subject}, parked {setting}, {light}, {atmosphere}; keep the complete truck and enough landscape visible to establish depth, expose for a dark moody frame with controlled highlights and readable shadow detail, with a static camera or barely perceptible natural drift, photographed like an ordinary understated phone clip rather than a polished product render, {subject_state}

reject: milky haze, pale high-key daylight, or a washed-out low-contrast grade
synthetic sharpening halos or product-render crispness
crushed-black featureless body or window slabs
near-duplicate door, wheel, mirror, or bed fragments across accounts

truck.note: PRIMARY truck bible reset by Smaths 2026-07-22 to the actual early iPhone-Mirroring winners and darkened again 2026-08-14 after the bright batch underperformed. Hailuo is landscape-only, so the complete 16:9 source is fitted into one vertical blurred canvas; positional five-crop output was removed after the 2026-08-27 canary proved it geometrically amputates the required complete truck. WINNER_VISUAL_REFERENCE.md remains the admission authority: dark low-exposure natural truck views, muted lake/grass/field/forest settings, controlled highlights, restrained color, and ordinary camera softness. Washed-out daylight and the former crisp featureless side-on desert product-render look are rejected. OCR plus strict visual and winner-reference QA remain mandatory; reject badges, occupants, plates, morphs, duplicates, and visual-profile misses.
